evidence.note: Initial plans enumerate the full subsystem set and state a foundation-first order (health, SigV4 auth, storage before multipart/versioning/config, then console/admin/workers) — sensible dependency-aware sequencing but expressed as a flat repeated to-do, not a milestone hierarchy with done-checks.
Plans are repetitive 'append the next handler, then the next' enumerations restating remaining work each step; no per-subsystem acceptance criteria articulated as milestones.
Repeated full rewrites/corruption from a monolithic single-file approach show work was not sized into verifiable increments — counter to the high anchors' 'verifiable increment' sizing.
Rough done-sense via compile-check + boto3 round-trips per feature (basic CRUD, multipart, tagging/versioning), giving an approximate 'when is this done' but not explicit milestone acceptance gates.
Ends with three Submit-complete attempts while listing known unresolved bugs and a possibly-down server, indicating the plan did not carry through to verified milestone completion across the horizon.

reasoning: The agent enumerated the major subsystems and tackled them in a broadly sensible foundation-first order (auth/storage/health before multipart/versioning/console), with a rough compile-plus-boto3 sense of when each feature worked — squarely anchor 5. It never rose to anchor 8: plans were flat, repetitive enumerations without an explicit dependency-aware milestone hierarchy or concrete per-milestone acceptance checks, and the monolithic-file approach with repeated rewrites shows work was not sized into verifiable increments. It stays above anchor 3 because ordering rationale and rough done-criteria are present.
